package heldcallback

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"slices"
	"sync"

	"example.test/auth"
	"example.test/hooks"
	"example.test/httperr"
)

type Handlers struct{ once sync.Once }

// sync.Once runs its callback at most once in the process, so a second
// request passes no check at all.
func (h *Handlers) GetAfterOnce(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var err error
	h.once.Do(func() { err = auth.Require(r.Context()) })
	if err != nil {
		httperr.Write(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httperr.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, []int{1})
}

// A registration keeps its callback for later, and runs none of it now.
func (h *Handlers) GetAfterARegistration(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if err := hooks.OnReady(func(ctx context.Context) error { return auth.Require(ctx) }); err != nil {
		httperr.Write(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httperr.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, []int{1})
}

// An iterator calls its callback once per row, so over none it calls it no
// time.
func (h *Handlers) GetAfterAnIterator(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	rows := []int{1}
	refused := slices.ContainsFunc(rows, func(int) bool {
		if allowed, _ := auth.IndividualPerformanceOf(r.Context()); !allowed {
			return true
		}
		return false
	})
	if refused {
		httperr.Write(w, r, auth.OffError{})
		return
	}
	httperr.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, rows)
}
